column3: “A young lion it was” is rendered “He became a lion.”
“She waited” is rendered “as she waited”; the verb is uncertain.
“It knew its widows” is rendered “he destroyed their fortified towers,” following a slightly different reading. The meaning is uncertain.
“In your blood” is rendered “in your vineyard,” following a slightly different reading.
“Above between branches” is rendered “above the clouds”; the word can mean either.
The Hebrew says “from the branch of its shoots, it consumed its fruit”; NASB has “It has consumed its shoots and fruit.”
